A deal mechanism is one that lands in a Deals API `Deal` (§ 1.1).
`embedded`: the ad is recorded into the content or aired in a live program, so everyone who receives that content receives that ad.
`non_guaranteed`: the seller reserves nothing.
A host read recorded into new episodes of a podcast: a buyer's composed record (§ 4.1.1) of a line item issued to it (§ 4.3), before its `commit`, with `retention` and no per-listener targeting.
See `examples/line-item-podcast-embedded.yaml`.
See `examples/line-item-ctv-live-series.yaml`.
A seven-game series sold as `programs`, with the games that may not be played outside the base rate.
The `assent[]` entries name version 1, and the digest is over that line item alone (§ 4.1.2).
The other stays `published` at version 2, with a hold, so the proposal stays `published` (§ 4.3.3).
A `change_requests[]` entry records a notice to cancel part of the agreed line item (§ 5.6.6).
One line item is agreed at version 1, with a commitment under one of two `pricing[]` entries.
Its buyer writes `selected[]` and `value`, and `agreed_rate` follows from the options in effect (§ 5.6).
See `examples/proposal-issued.yaml`.
§§ 6.9 and 6.10 show a buyer's composed record (§ 4.1.1) of a line item issued to it (§ 4.3), before its `commit`.
Its `line_items[]` holds the line items of §§ 6.2 to 6.4, 6.7, and 6.11, which are extracts of it.
Shows `selectable` audiences with per-option pricing, `pricing[]` alternatives in two currencies, cancellation options, `settable` bounds, and a `delivery_type` per mechanism.

Shows priced cancellation options at three `notice_duration` values, `break_position` with priced pre-roll and first-in-pod options (§ 5.2.3), server-side insertion in `placement.ssai` (§ 5.2.2), `format_specs` entries, two pinned to a format registry version and one defined by the seller (§ 5.4), and `keywords` accepted only as `best_effort` (§ 5.5).
Shows `placement.feed` on a music stream, a line item priced by market, a cancellation fee that steps with notice before the start, and priced exclusivity terms.
See `examples/proposal-package.yaml`, and the bonus alone in `examples/line-item-ctv-bonus.yaml`.
See `examples/manifest.json`.
The display line item is `registry_gated`, so it is not listed.
Shows `placement` on in-app rewarded video, with OMID support that lets a buyer select a third-party `measurement_source`.
See `examples/line-item-rewarded-video.yaml`.

Shows a custom proposal after the seller counters a request and accepts a commitment: matching `assent[]` entries over one `record_digest` (§ 4.1.1, § 4.1.2), which covers the `digest` of each document in `terms_refs[]` (§ 5.8), the history that led there (§ 4.3), and `change_requests[]` entries outside the digest, one for each line item, the second a deal with no Order (§ 4.4).
See `examples/proposal-agreed.yaml`.

Shows a buyer's composed record (§ 4.1.1) of a line item issued to it (§ 4.3), before its `commit`, with its `commitment`: a CPM priced on impressions, with the multiplier's source, data release, and settlement rule in `delivery_counting.impression_multiplier` (§ 5.6.4).
See `examples/line-item-dooh.yaml`.
Buyer–seller relationships are expressed as issued proposals (`visibility: named`, `eligible_buyers[]` set to that buyer, with the negotiated `pricing[]`) plus the buyer agent's business rules.
`agreement` and `terms_refs[]` (§ 5.10, § 5.8) point at the agreement and terms a line item is executed under; IO generation happens through connectors.
Each has its own `proposal_id` per counterparty or destination, and may carry `proposal_template_id` (§ 4.1) to trace it back to its template and `issued_from` to trace it back to a shared proposal.
Buyer-specific terms, such as annual rates and named visibility, live on the issued proposal's line items: `visibility: named`, `eligible_buyers[]` and their own `pricing[]`.
`description`, `media_kit_detail`, `best_for[]` and `seasonality_notes` are what a model needs to decide whether to look further.
`channel` is the discriminator.
Fields such as `placement`, `programs`, `break_position`, and the DOOH property keys apply only where a channel needs them, and `format_specs` carries what is channel-specific about creative shape.
Must a manifest response carry both `ETag` and `Last-Modified`, or is either enough?
This draft also doesn't state what a `credit` is worth.
A `format_specs` entry can copy a registry version or be defined by the seller (§ 5.4), so half the declared channels have only seller-defined specs today.
`environments.available[]` needs validation against real inventory.
The OpenDirect 2.1 ChangeRequest has no structured statement of any other change, only free-text `comments` (§ 4.4).
A package (§ 4.1.4) covers bundle purchases without a `min_line_items` count.
`spec_version` names the release a document follows, and § 2.5 makes a key the receiver's release does not list invalid.
How does a `change_requests[]` entry state a change other than a cancellation?
A `Line.productid` would be one use: an agreed record doesn't say which OpenDirect `Product` it books.
Every `Amount` on a line item is on one basis (§ 5.6).
`cancellation` states a notice to cancel.
Once one line item guarantees `viewable_rate` and another `completion_rate`, there is no normalised way for a buying agent to compare or optimise across them. 3.0 doesn't cover it.
A `spec_ref` names a registry by domain alone: this draft doesn't say which registry that is or how to fetch an entry.
A `commitment.amount` of 80,000.00 at an `agreed_rate` of 24.00 `CPM` buys 3,333,333 impressions if 24.00 is what the seller invoices.
Should `billing.payment_terms` and `billing.invoicing_party` be repeated on every line item, given they are usually identical across a seller's shelf?

It MUST contain, per line item:
A full fetch MUST return it.
`catalog_ref` values MUST remain unresolved in a summary.
A catalog response MAY return it.
When a proposal reaches status `agreed`, every `catalog_ref` MUST be replaced by its resolved value in the stored record, so the committed artifact is self-contained and immutable.
References MUST be version-pinned.
A field MUST carry either an inline value or a `catalog_ref`, never both.
References MUST resolve during discovery.
Any field whose value is drawn from a seller-maintained catalog MAY carry a reference in place of an inline value:
A catalog entry MUST be immutable once referenced; a change creates a new version.
A buyer MAY select and commit a subset of a proposal's line items, unless the proposal explicitly mandates linked execution through its binding terms.
Each line item MUST be fully self-contained.
Every field marked `selectable` MUST declare:
A field marked `selectable` that carries a bare value and no `available[]` MUST be treated as `seller-set`.
MAY be empty
A field marked `settable` that carries a bare value and no bounds MUST be treated as `seller-set`.
Every field marked `settable` MUST declare its bounds: either `allowed[]` (an enumerated set) or `min` / `max` (a numeric or date range).
Because audiences, properties and formats are `selectable`, `addressable_scale` and `availability` MUST be recomputed against the buyer's actual selection.
An unset `selectable` or `settable` field takes its declared `included[]` or default, and that default MUST be explicit in the proposal.
The seller sets it and MAY revise it while status is `draft` or `published`.
REQUIRED.
A request carrying an `idempotency_key` already seen MUST return the original result and MUST NOT create a second commitment.
OPTIONAL.
Seller declares a ceiling; a buyer MAY request above it
A seller MAY offer the same inventory through more than one
Each line item lands in the one its `transaction_mechanism` maps to:
Custom proposal — built in response to a buyer's agent brief, referenced via `brief_ref`.
Full Representation — every field, with all `catalog_ref` values resolved.
plus, from the parent proposal: `proposal_id` · `seller_name` · `description` · `valid_from` · `valid_until`.

`line_item_id` · `channel` · `content_detail` · property names · `formats.included[]` · `pricing.cost_method` · `pricing.gross_rate` · `min_spend` · `addressable_scale` · `committed_metrics[]` · `transaction_mechanism`
A `catalog_ref` is not inheritance.
`pricing` generalises it to every dimension a seller is willing to vary, and replaces it.
`audience_pricing` in earlier drafts was the precedent for this pattern — it expressed "if you change X, the price moves by Y".
A bare value means the field is `seller-set`.
Frozen when status becomes `agreed`.
Transitions: `none` → `requested` → `held` → (`expired` | `released` | `converted`).
`converted` is terminal and occurs when the line item reaches `agreed`.
Shows `selectable` audiences with per-option pricing, a catalog reference, a buyer commitment, and `settable` bounds.
Channel support cost one new field and one generalisation — `channel`, and `committed_metrics[]` as tuples — rather than a schema fork per channel.
`description`, `specifications`, `best_for` and `seasonality_notes` are what a model needs to decide whether to look further.
`specs` delegates to a registry that cannot currently answer for half the declared channels.
Do seller catalogs (`catalog_ref`) belong in 3.0, or should the object stay fully inline until a later version?
Is a `min_line_items` field needed on the proposal to require a bundle purchase, or is that left to buyer discretion?
`environments[]` needs validation against real inventory.
Once one line item guarantees `viewable_rate` and another `completion_rate`, there is no normalised way for a buying agent to compare or optimise across them.
Should `payment_terms` and `invoicing_party` be catalog references rather than repeated on every line item, given they are usually identical across a seller's shelf?
